label: GlusterFS storage interoperability
summary: Prepare bounded observations of admitted GlusterFS volumes, peers and recovery state through a Core-owned storage provider.
core_boundary: No gluster shell, arbitrary brick path or cluster-wide root authority is delegated. Basic local storage stays free; distributed storage is not treated as a generic object bucket. This is a design-only connector proposal. Essential hosting, current actor and tenant authorization, native service drivers and recovery remain in the free Core. No production interface, publisher trust, installation or effectful capability is established by this metadata.
acceptance: Qualify release maintenance, artifact provenance and an exact Core provider profile before claiming a supported host/API matrix; record peer, volume, brick and tenant ownership.
Observe quorum, health and pending/split-brain healing separately from effects; never auto-select an authoritative copy, force healing or detach a peer from a plugin decision.
Exercise network partitions, full volumes, mount dependencies and interrupted recovery; preserve source data and require separate backup/recovery review before removal or destructive repair.

Declare observation-only, import or externally managed ownership before any integration request. Refuse competing writers for Core-owned resources; ownership handoff requires an authorized inventory, admission review and recovery plan.

Before implementation, qualify an explicitly selected provider/interface revision, supported compatibility matrix, immutable package provenance, dependency inventory and licensing model; no release is admitted by this proposal.

Enforce current Core actor, tenant and capability checks at each admitted request; keep credentials in scoped secret references, redact diagnostics and reject arbitrary destinations, shell commands or host/container sockets.

Demonstrate that disablement, removal, provider outage and commercial entitlement loss preserve essential Core access, hosted workloads, local audit and recovery; retain owned data unless a separately authorized purge is requested.
